title: Letter-forms chart and handwriting sheet
subject: Arabic
unit: Spring 1: Common vocabulary: numbers, colours, clothes and shapes
source: Written for arabic/y7 lesson 9 (Letter-forms chart and handwriting sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 9: Bridge: the Arabic letters and how they join. Read the Arabic aloud, then do the tasks. Write in Arabic with all the harakat.

panels.title: Letters that do not join forward
points: ا د ذ ر ز و
They join to the letter before, never after
دَرْس (dars): د and ر stand apart from the next letter

model.title: Write كَتَبَ (kataba, he wrote) from ك + ت + ب

parts.text: Join: كتب, then add the vowels: كَتَبَ

panels.title: Dictation routine
points: Say the letters as you write

questions.q: Join the letters: ق + ل + م
Why is there a gap in دار?
questions.a: د and ا do not join to the next letter.

questions.q: Core: Dictation: write the four words the teacher reads (بَاب، دَرْس، قَلَم، وَرْدَة), then copy each three times neatly.
Extend: Join: ك + ت + ا + ب and م + د + ر + س + ة.
Stretch: Find three words in Surah al-Ikhlas that have a non-joining letter.
Which letter never joins to the next letter?
questions.a: B) ر. ر is one of the six: ا د ذ ر ز و.

questions.q: How many forms can one Arabic letter have? A) 2 B) 4 C) 6
Big question: why do Arabic letters change shape?
questions.a: Because letters join; their form depends on whether they are at the start, middle or end of a word.
